sections.html:
Walk-in payments go to 200 E 4th Street in Woodbine; by mail, use PO Box 698. Phone 912-576-3248 between 9 and 5 on weekdays. Appraisal lives in a different department, where assessors named by the county commissioners field value questions at 912-576-3241.

Sellers should know that the tax office will not split a year's tax between buyer and seller. The tax stays the owner's liability. Your closing attorney or title company calculates the division and asks the office what is owed on the parcel.

sections.h2: When the bill arrives and when it is due
sections.html:
Mid-September is when bills go out, with payment due 60 days later. Whoever owned the property on January 1 of that tax year is the one billed, so forward the notice to your buyer if you sold afterward. Still no bill on October 15? Phone 912-576-3248.

State revenue guidance for Camden mentions December 20 as the usual statewide deadline, which a county can shift or split into installments. Taxpayers also get 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest starts. The local schedule wins, so trust the date on your own statement.

sections.h2: Late charges and how a lien builds
sections.html:
A bill is delinquent from the day after it is due. The interest rate is the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent yearly, a partial month is charged as a full month, and the minimum charge is $1. A flat 5% penalty applies at 120 days overdue, and again at 240, 360 and 480. Homestead bills of $500 or less escape the penalty, and so do new owners who lived outside Georgia, never received a bill and pay within a year.

What follows a missed Camden County due date
WhenWhat happens
Day after the due dateInterest begins
Week after the due date30-day lien warning is mailed
About a week after the warning period endsLien is filed with the Clerk of Superior Court, adding a filing cost of $28.50 to $33.50
120, 240, 360 and 480 days overdue5% penalty each time
After filingA tax sale can be scheduled

sections.h2: Can I get my house back after a tax sale?
sections.html:
Yes, but only for a limited time. The tax lien dates back to the January 1 valuation and ranks ahead of every other lien. On each December 31 the tax commissioner has to issue an execution on delinquent accounts, telling the levying officer to collect or to levy and sell.

To redeem, you repay the winning bid and any later taxes the buyer covered, then add 20% of that total for year one, or part of it. Every further year or part adds 10%. Once twelve months pass, the buyer can serve notice that ends redemption for good. Even then, the earliest anyone can take possession is one year and forty-five days after the deed.

With that timeline in mind, selling before the sale date usually leaves you more equity than waiting.

Your 45 days begin with a Notice of Reassessment. Address the appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors and get it postmarked within that window. Because assessed value equals 40% of January 1 market value, a rising market pushes assessed value up too.

If you overpaid, there is a separate route: ask in writing for a refund of tax assessed or collected in error, within three years of paying.

  • Returns go to the county tax office between January 1 and April 1.
  • Homestead applications are taken year-round, but April 1 is the cutoff for that year.
  • Skipping the application is treated as waiving the exemption.

Pull together deeds, survey papers and any receipts for improvements before you apply or appeal, so the office can match its records to your file in one visit.

sections.h2: Do Kingsland, St. Marys and Woodbine send their own tax bills?
sections.html:
Maybe. It depends on the address. A city can levy its own property tax and have its clerk bill it, unless the city and county agreed to combine everything on one county statement. Vehicle tax is the exception: only the county tax commissioner collects it.

Ask the Woodbine tax office if a city bill applies to your address, then ask the city clerk for any balance, because unpaid city tax can stall a closing as readily as county tax.

Two more rules apply around a purchase. A mobile home needs a county location permit within 30 days of placement, then again every January 1 to April 1. A long-term note secured by real estate must be recorded in the county within 90 days and carries intangible recording tax of $1.50 for each $500 of the note.

sections.h2: If you are behind on Camden County taxes
sections.html:
Being late does not stop you from selling. The lien rides along with the property, so the buyer's title company will insist that it be paid, and the usual way is to pay it from your sale proceeds at closing. Ask the tax office for the exact balance, including interest, any 5% penalties and the lien filing cost if a lien has been recorded.

The sooner you act, the less it costs. Each missed 120-day mark adds another 5%, and once a tax sale is on the calendar your choices shrink. A fast sale to a buyer who pays cash, with the payoff handled at closing, is one way to clear the account before the next step in the schedule above arrives.

sections.h2: What Camden's housing market looks like
sections.html:
Georgia's southeastern corner belongs to Camden, bordered by Glynn County north and Florida's Nassau County south. Kingsland is its largest city, with St. Marys and Woodbine rounding out the list, and Interstate 95 and U.S. 17 both cross it. The Navy submarine base at Kings Bay is a major local presence, and Cumberland Island National Seashore lies inside the county.

About 60,143 people lived here as of July 2025. Owners occupy 67.8% of homes, a typical owned home is valued at $261,400, rent runs $1,235 a month, and 446 permits for new housing were issued in 2025.

sections.h2: Steps to settle taxes when you sell
sections.html:
Begin with a call to 912-576-3248 to get the balance on your parcel and learn whether an earlier year is open. A house inside a city needs a second figure from the city clerk. Pass both numbers to the closing attorney or title company, who settles them from your proceeds and splits the current year with the buyer.

If a bill never came, do not wait for it. Interest builds anyway, so call early. A cash sale may close faster than a financed one, but it needs the same tax figures.

faqs.q: Does the Woodbine tax office divide the bill between buyer and seller?
faqs.a: No, the office stays out of prorating, and the tax remains the owner's liability. The closing attorney or title company works out the split from the balance the office confirms.

faqs.q: I never received a Camden County statement. What now?
faqs.a: Phone 912-576-3248. Owners with nothing in hand by October 15 are asked to call. Interest keeps building on a late balance whether or not the bill reached you.

faqs.q: How fast does a Camden County lien follow a missed due date?
faqs.a: A 30-day warning goes out the week after the due date. About a week after that period ends, the lien is filed at the Clerk of Superior Court, and a $28.50 to $33.50 filing cost lands on your bill.

faqs.q: After a Camden County tax sale, can the owner redeem?
faqs.a: Yes. Repay the buyer's price plus 20% for year one and 10% for each year after. The right stays open until the buyer finishes the notice steps that bar it, which can start twelve months after the sale.

faqs.q: Is there a late penalty on a small Camden County homestead bill?
faqs.a: No. A homestead bill of $500 or less is excused from the 5% penalty, though interest still runs at the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent.
